claim: Ivacaftor improves lung function in cystic fibrosis patients with a G551D mutation
gold_rationale: Documented clinical and regulatory consensus. The pivotal Phase 3 placebo-controlled RCT STRIVE (Ramsey NEJM 2011, NCT00909532, n=167, ages ≥12) showed a 10.6 percentage-point treatment effect on absolute change in percent-predicted FEV1 through week 24, sustained to 48 weeks (P<0.001), plus reduced pulmonary exacerbations, improved CFQ-R, weight gain, and −48 mmol/L sweat chloride. The parallel pediatric Phase 3 RCT ENVISION (NCT00909727, n=52, ages 6–11) reproduced the effect with a 12.5pp primary-endpoint ppFEV1 treatment effect (P<0.001; ~10pp at 48 weeks). The NIHR HTA systematic review (Whiting 2014) pooled both RCTs plus the open-label extension, confirming ~10.5pp (adults) and 10.0pp (children) ppFEV1 improvement across all subgroups. Real-world G551D cohorts (severe-disease named-patient series; Scottish paediatric review) reproduced significant FEV1 gains. On this evidence FDA approved KALYDECO (ivacaftor) on 31 Jan 2012 for CF patients ≥6 years with the G551D mutation — the first drug targeting the underlying CFTR defect. Directly on the claimed ppFEV1 outcome (no surrogate substitution) with concordant RCT + regulatory + real-world evidence, the verdict is Supported.
outcome: ppFEV1 lung function (absolute change in percent-predicted FEV1)
population: Cystic fibrosis patients with a G551D-CFTR gating mutation (on ≥1 allele)

baseline.text: Yes. Ivacaftor (Kalydeco) markedly improves lung function in CF patients with a G551D gating mutation. The pivotal STRIVE trial (Ramsey et al., NEJM 2011) in patients aged 12 and older showed a 10.6 percentage-point improvement in percent-predicted FEV1 versus placebo through 24 weeks, sustained to 48 weeks, along with fewer pulmonary exacerbations, better quality of life, and weight gain. The pediatric ENVISION trial (ages 6-11) showed a comparable ~10-12 percentage-point FEV1 benefit. These results led to FDA approval of ivacaftor in 2012 specifically for the G551D mutation, and it is the standard of care and regulatory/clinical consensus for this population.

rows.citation: Ramsey BW, Davies J, McElvaney NG, et al. A CFTR potentiator in patients with cystic fibrosis and the G551D mutation (STRIVE). N Engl J Med. 2011;365(18):1663-72. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa1105185. NCT00909532.
rows.integrity_note: Pivotal Phase 3 double-blind placebo-controlled RCT; primary endpoint met with P<0.001; industry-funded (Vertex) with Cystic Fibrosis Foundation collaborator. Verified against PubMed metadata and ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00909532.
rows.finding: Absolute change in ppFEV1 through week 24 was 10.6 percentage points greater with ivacaftor than placebo (P<0.001); effect noted by 2 weeks and sustained through week 48; also 55% fewer pulmonary exacerbations, +2.7 kg weight, -48.1 mmol/L sweat chloride.

rows.citation: ENVISION: Phase 3 RCT of ivacaftor in CF subjects aged 6-11 with G551D mutation (n=52). Davies J, et al. Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2013;187(11):1219-25 (PMID:23590265). ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00909727.
rows.integrity_note: Registered Phase 3 double-blind placebo-controlled pediatric RCT with posted results; primary endpoint ppFEV1 through Week 24. Verified via ClinicalTrials.gov and PubMed (PMID:23590265).
rows.finding: Pediatric (6-11y) G551D RCT: primary endpoint treatment effect on ppFEV1 through Week 24 was 12.5 percentage points vs placebo (P<0.001), evident by 2 weeks and sustained to Week 48 (~10pp at 48wk in HTA pooling); +2.8 kg weight, -53.5 mmol/L sweat chloride.

rows.citation: Whiting P, Al M, Burgers L, et al. Ivacaftor for CF and the G551D mutation: a systematic review and cost-effectiveness analysis (NIHR HTA). Health Technol Assess. 2014;18(18):1-106. DOI:10.3310/hta18180. PROSPERO CRD42012002516.
rows.integrity_note: Independent NIHR-funded systematic review synthesizing both pivotal RCTs plus the open-label extension; no formal meta-analysis due to sparse trials but consistent effect. Verified via PubMed (PMID:24656117).
rows.finding: Pooled RCT evidence: mean ppFEV1 difference 10.5pp (95% CI 8.5-12.5) in adults and 10.0pp (95% CI 4.5-15.5) in children at 48 weeks; improvements across all subgroups (age, sex, region, lung function), maintained in the open-label extension.

rows.citation: Hebestreit H, Sauer-Heilborn A, Fischer R, et al. Effects of ivacaftor on severely ill patients with CF carrying a G551D mutation. J Cyst Fibros. 2013;12(6):599-603. DOI:10.1016/j.jcf.2013.05.006.
rows.integrity_note: CORRECTION: this is a RETROSPECTIVE named-patient cohort (abstract and MeSH 'Retrospective Studies'), not prospective; schema enum lacks a retrospective-cohort option. Severe patients (ppFEV1<40%) excluded from pivotal trials; response variable but net positive. Verified via PubMed (PMID:23757359).
rows.finding: In severe G551D CF (ppFEV1<40%, n=14 named-patient program, Germany), ppFEV1 rose significantly by mean 5.2±5.6 points (relative +19.7±22.1%) after ivacaftor (P<0.01); extends benefit beyond the trial-eligible population, though response was variable.

rows.citation: Dryden C, Wilkinson J, Young D, Brooker RJ (on behalf of SPCFMCN). Impact of 12 months treatment with ivacaftor on Scottish paediatric CF patients with the G551D mutation: a review. Arch Dis Child. 2016;103(1):68-70. DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2015-310420.
rows.integrity_note: Real-world national Scottish paediatric review (SPCFMCN); small cohort, statistically significant results comparable to RCTs. NOTE: exact N not stated in abstract — n_int is approximate/unconfirmed. Verified paper exists via PubMed (PMID:27288428) and BMJ/ADC.
rows.finding: Real-world Scottish paediatric G551D cohort: statistically significant improvements in FEV1 and BMI and reduced sweat chloride over 12 months, comparable to published RCT data; suggested reduced IV/oral antibiotic use.

rows.citation: FDA. KALYDECO (ivacaftor) approval, NDA 203188, initial U.S. approval 31 Jan 2012 (accessdata.fda.gov 203188Orig1s000). Indicated for CF patients age 6+ with a G551D mutation in CFTR; approval based on STRIVE (NCT00909532) + ENVISION (NCT00909727). Vertex press release 2012-01-31.
rows.integrity_note: CORRECTION: source_id changed from the duplicated STRIVE trial DOI to the real regulatory anchor (NDA 203188 / STRIVE NCT). FDA marketing approval based on STRIVE+ENVISION; ppFEV1 improvement is the pivotal efficacy basis. Approval date 31 Jan 2012 and age-6+ G551D indication independently verified via FDA accessdata NDA 203188 and Vertex/PRNewswire release.
rows.finding: FDA approved ivacaftor (Kalydeco) on 31 Jan 2012 for CF patients aged 6+ with the G551D mutation — the first drug targeting the underlying CFTR defect; approval driven by the ~10-12.5pp ppFEV1 improvement in the two pivotal RCTs (approx. 3 months after NDA submission).
